intro: Entropy measures how much uncertainty remains in a categorical distribution. Certain outcomes carry no uncertainty while balanced alternatives carry more.
task: Compute Shannon entropy in natural-log units, treating a zero-probability outcome as a zero contribution.
requirements: probabilities is a nonnegative vector whose sum is one within absolute tolerance 1e-8.
Return the scalar -sum(p*log(p)) over strictly positive entries. Use natural logarithms, so the result is in nats.
Return zero for a certain outcome. Do not add epsilon or normalize an invalid probability vector.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Find the structure
hints.body: Think of entropy as expected surprise, so each logarithm needs its own probability weight.

hints.title: Build the calculation
hints.body: Select positive probabilities before applying logarithms; zero-mass entries have zero contribution by continuity.

explanation: Each outcome contributes its probability times its surprise, -log(p). A probability-zero event has zero expected contribution by the limiting value of p log(p).
For k equally likely outcomes the result is log(k). Concentrating all mass on one outcome removes uncertainty and produces zero.
